title: Application of Atomic Force Microscopy to Detect Early Osteoarthritis
protocol: Take articular cartilage samples from the load-bearing zone of the femoral condyles after tissue resection.
Store the cartilage samples in serum-free DMEM with 2% penicillin-streptomycin and 1.2% amphotericin B prior to use.
Ensure that samples are used for AFM measurements within 24 hours after surgery to avoid artifacts due to tissue swelling.
Cut the articular cartilage as a whole from the subchondral bone with a scalpel.
Embed the cartilage sample in water-soluble embedding medium on the cryotome knob that freezes under low temperature in the cryotome device.
Place the tissue embedded for the cryosections such that the top layer (i.e., articular surface) of the cartilage faces the blade.
Ensure the tissue is fully covered by the embedding medium.
Section the tissue at a thickness of 35 µm from the topmost layer (i.e., articular surface) of the articular cartilage using a standard cryotome.
Collect the sections on a glass slide.
Rinse the sections 3 times with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to remove the water-soluble embedding medium.
Gently glue the 35 µm thick cartilage sections with biocompatible sample glue onto tissue culture dishes compatible with the AFM device.
Place 2-3 drops of glue on the tissue culture dish at the location where the edge of the section will end up.
Put the cartilage section on the glue and allow it to stick firmly to the surface of the tissue culture dish.
Spread the tissue on the dispersed spots of glue so that it is fixed to the surface of the cell culture dish as soon as excess water has dried up.
Measure only that portion of the sample that is far from the glued area to eliminate the possibility of the glue interfering with measurements.
Incubate the sections at room temperature (RT) for 2 min to allow the glue and tissue to bond properly.
Cover the sections with Leibovitz's L-15 medium without L-glutamine and without Sodium bicarbonate so that they are fully submerged.
Place the Petri dish with the glued sections in the standard cell culture incubator at 37 °C until measurements are performed.
Place the cantilever on the glass block specified for air measurements.
Fix the cantilever with a spring and mount the glass block on the AFM head.
Dilute the microspheres in 100% ethanol (100 particles/10 µL).
Ultrasonicate the diluted microspheres for 10 s so that the microspheres are separated and do not clump together.
Clean a glass slide with 70% ethanol.
Mount the cleaned glass slide on the sample holder on the AFM device.
Place 2 µL of the microsphere suspension in the middle of the slide.
Place 2 µL of glue near the microsphere suspension.
Let the ethanol liquid in the microsphere suspension air-dry, leaving the microspheres in place.
Dip the cantilever manually into the glue with the help of the stepper motor in 10 µm steps until the tip is covered by glue.
Retract the cantilever again by 100 µm.
Move the cantilever towards the microspheres and position the cantilever tip directly above a single microsphere.
Run a force spectroscopy measurement to dip the cantilever tip onto the selected microsphere with the parameters shown in Table 1.
Mount the cantilever on a glass block.
Incubate the cantilever at 65°C for 2 hours.
Dry the cantilever overnight at room temperature.
Adjust a glass block for measuring in a liquid environment on the AFM holder.
Mount the selected cantilever on the surface of the glass block using tweezers.
Ensure the AFM tip with the microsphere protrudes over the polished optical plane.
Slide the metallic spring into the groove of the glass block to stabilize the cantilever.
Clamp the top of the cantilever with the spring using tweezers.
Place the glass block with the mounted cantilever on the AFM head and secure it with the integrated locking mechanism.
Ensure the spring is facing the left side for correct orientation.
Mount the AFM head with the cantilever onto the AFM device.
Place the Petri dish onto the AFM sample holder.
Turn on the Petri dish heater and set it at 37 °C.
Allow the tissue culture dish to reach optimal temperature for 20 min.
Mount a protecting foil on the base of the cantilever assembly.
Open the software followed by the laser alignment window and approach parameter settings.
Turn on the stepper motor, the laser light, and the CCD-camera.
Visualize the cantilever using the CCD-camera.
Lower the cantilever in 100 µm steps until fully submerged in the medium.
Direct the laser on top of the cantilever using adjustment screws.
Do not overwind the screws to avoid damaging the laser alignment mechanism.
View the cantilever from below and position the laser beam from above onto the cantilever.
Adjust the laser beam using the screws in the AFM device so that it falls onto the center of the photodetector.
Monitor the position of the laser beam using the laser alignment function continuously.
The detector converts the deflection of the reflected laser beam by the cantilever into an electrical signal.
After adjusting the laser-cantilever, ensure the Sum signal is 1 V or above and lateral and vertical deflections are close to 0.
If values are not met, adjust the photodetector accordingly.
Run a scanner Approach with given approach parameters in Table 2 to reach the surface on the AFM dish for measurements.
Retract the cantilever by 100 µm once the bottom of the tissue culture dish is reached.
Set up RUN parameters and adjust according to those displayed in Table 3.
Click the RUN button to start a measurement and obtain a calibration force-distance curve.
Select the region for a linear fit of the retracted curve on the obtained calibration force-distance curve within the software.
Set the temperature variable at 37 °C in the software for calibration.
Identify chondrocyte patterns in the cartilage section under a phase contrast microscope integrated in the AFM system.
Observe single strings, double strings, small clusters, and big clusters to assess tissue degeneration.
Measure two sites per chosen pattern per matrix type (PCM or ECM).
Perform nine measurement repetitions on each measurement site.
Place the cantilever in close proximity to the cells for PCM measurements.
Select a region without any cells for ECM measurements.
Position the cantilever 100 µm above the tissue as the starting position.
Focus on the PCM or ECM of the pattern and fix the computer mouse at that point.
Move the tip of the probe to the point previously fixed by the computer arrow.
Start the measurements with RUN, using the set point parameter obtained by calibration.
